text: SOC 2 and ISO 27001 both require real evidence, and both Azure and AWS build tools that generate most of it automatically from your actual configuration, instead of leaving you to assemble everything by hand. This lesson covers four real tools — two on each side — and what each one genuinely does.

Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager gives your organization a compliance score against a chosen framework, like ISO 27001, NIST CSF, or GDPR, and lists the specific actions still outstanding — both technical ones it can verify automatically, like MFA enforcement, and non-technical ones, like whether a written incident response policy actually exists. Azure Policy regulatory compliance initiatives are what actually feed the Defender for Cloud compliance dashboard from Chapter 5: built-in bundles of policy definitions mapped to named frameworks, continuously evaluating your real resource configurations against each control.

Assign an Azure Policy initiative like "ISO 27001:2013" to a subscription, and it evaluates your actual resources against every control in that framework, reporting the result straight into the same Regulatory Compliance view from Chapter 5. On the AWS side, a Config conformance pack does the equivalent job: deploy one pack and an entire framework's worth of Config rules starts evaluating your whole account at once.

AWS Audit Manager takes a continuous-evidence approach instead of a one-time score. Choose a prebuilt framework — SOC 2, PCI DSS, CIS Benchmarks, and ISO 27001 are all options — and it automatically pulls evidence from AWS Config, CloudTrail, and Security Hub findings, organized by control. By the time a real audit starts, most of that evidence is already sitting there waiting, instead of being scrambled together the week before.

Next lesson: using everything in this chapter to actually prepare for an audit — gathering configuration exports, access logs, and policy documents ahead of time, and the common findings, like stale access and missing logging, that catch cloud teams who wait until the auditor asks.
